headline: Highest risk is data leakage: Haystack’s broad egress/MCP can feed Perplexity’s vendor-hosted browsing and uploaded-document pipeline, creating default exfiltration and compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack exposes MCP and REST APIs, so it can pass content into Perplexity’s browsing/search workflows. Perplexity’s vendor-hosted Pro Search and uploaded-document analysis can treat incoming text as context, making instruction smuggling plausible. The pairwise bridge is documented only indirectly, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Haystack forwards untrusted retrieved text into Perplexity prompts or uploads
IF Perplexity renders retrieved content as instructions instead of data
mitigations: Strip or delimit retrieved text before handoff
Add a fixed system prompt that ignores instructions in retrieved content
Disable MCP routes that accept arbitrary external content
Require human review for any prompt containing web or file text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and MCP, while Perplexity is vendor-hosted and processes search queries, browsing context, and uploaded PDFs/images. That creates a default path for sensitive workspace content to leave the operator’s environment and enter a third-party backend. The pair touches only anonymous usage stats on Haystack, but Perplexity’s broader data classes make leakage materially worse.
conditions: IF Haystack sends retrieved documents or prompts through MCP to Perplexity
IF Perplexity receives uploaded files or browsing context containing sensitive material
mitigations: Block sensitive documents from the Haystack→Perplexity path
Use a redaction step before any upload or query
Restrict Perplexity use to non-sensitive searches only
Log and review all outbound prompts for secrets
requires-engineering: add DLP enforcement on the integration boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack can call REST APIs and MCP servers, but it does not advertise filesystem write or git mutation. Perplexity is vendor-hosted with no host execution, no filesystem write, and no git state changes. Overlap exists mainly in read/query surfaces, so write-write conflict is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF Haystack is wrapped in a separate tool that adds filesystem or git writes
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in shared workflows
Separate mutable resources by agent
Disable any wrapper that adds write access
Use per-agent service accounts for APIs

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG system that can generate retrieved facts, and Perplexity is an answer engine that produces cited responses from browsing context. If Haystack’s output is fed into Perplexity without verification, Perplexity may amplify retrieval errors into polished but wrong answers. The interaction is plausible from the profiles, but not directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Haystack output is used as authoritative input to Perplexity
IF Perplexity is asked to act on Haystack-generated facts without a verification step
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents
Require source citations for every forwarded claim
Compare Perplexity answers against original documents
Limit Haystack to retrieval-only mode for chained tasks

E_compliance.rationale: Haystack is open-source and only lists anonymous usage statistics, while Perplexity is closed-source, vendor-hosted, and processes search queries, uploaded documents, and browsing context. That creates a compliance mismatch risk around retention and residency for user content, even though no specific PHI or EU-only data class is documented here. The other agent is cited because the mismatch is pairwise.
conditions: IF regulated or region-bound data is sent through Perplexity
IF retention or residency requirements apply to uploaded documents or browsing context
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Perplexity workflows
Review Perplexity retention and residency settings before use
Use Haystack only for non-regulated retrieval tasks
Document a data-class allowlist for the pair
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
